programmes.d: An undead warthog sets her sights on Nami, Zorro and Sanji vanish without a trace, Franky and Robin battle an unbeatable army, and Luffy gets captured!

programmes.st: CHIVALRY REMAINS! THE TRAITOROUS ZOMBIE PROTECTS NAMI
programmes.d: A penguin zombie starts acting an awful lot like Sanji, Nami continues running for her life, and Robin and Franky buy some time by blowing up a bridge!

programmes.st: APPEARING FROM THE SKY! THAT MAN IS THE HUMMING SWORDSMAN!
programmes.d: Nami gives love advice to a zombie, Luffy finds himself face-to-face with Gecko Moria, and Robin gets caught in spooky spider web. Things look bleak for the Straw Hats until their skeleton friend lends a hand!

programmes.st: LUFFY'S EMERGENCY SITUATION! THE ULTIMATE SHADOW'S DESTINATION!
programmes.d: Brook strikes the final blow in his battle with the spider monkey, Gecko Moria's devious plan is revealed, and Luffy's escape attempt leads to the loss of something he can't live without!

programmes.st: THE WARRIOR KNOWN AS THE "DEVIL"!! THE MOMENT OF OARS' REVIVAL
programmes.d: Brook tells Franky and Robin the secret to slaying zombies, and Gecko Moria reveals the terrifying monster that will be the recipient of Luffy's shadow!

programmes.st: AWAKENING AFTER 500 YEARS!! OARS OPENS HIS EYES!!
programmes.d: Luffy's shadow is forced into the body of a monster, Usopp and Chopper get incinerated, and Nami is kidnapped by a zombie who wants to make her his wife!

programmes.st: A BELIEF WORTH BEGGING TO LIVE FOR!! BROOK DEFENDS HIS AFRO
programmes.d: Gecko Moria's minions struggle with the burden of feeding a giant zombie brought to life by Luffy's shadow. Meanwhile, Brook flashes back to a battle that almost cost him his beloved afro!

programmes.st: A MAN'S PROMISE NEVER DIES!! TO THE FRIEND WAITING UNDER THE DISTANT SKY
programmes.d: The freshly-revived trio of Luffy, Zoro, and Sanji discover that their shadows are missing, and Franky relates Brook's story about a promise he made to a very special whale!

programmes.st: I SWEAR TO GO SEE HIM!! BROOK AND THE CAPE OF PROMISE
programmes.d: Luffy and the Straw Hats flash back to the heartbreaking story of Laboon the abandoned whale, and Brook's battle with the zombie samurai reveals the reason behind his intense afro love!

programmes.st: FOOD, NAMI AND SHADOWS!! LUFFY'S ENRAGED COUNTERATTACK
programmes.d: Luffy sets out to regain his shadow and convince Brook to join the crew. Meanwhile, Sanji races to stop Nami's zombie wedding before it's too late!

programmes.st: USOPP'S THE STRONGEST? LEAVE ANYTHING NEGATIVE TO HIM
programmes.d: Usopp's naturally negative personality makes him the only Straw Hat who stands a chance against Perona's depressing army of ghosts, and Chopper prepares to do battle against his hero, Dr. Hogback!

programmes.st: THE GENERAL ZOMBIES ARE DOWN IN A FLASH!! OARS FEELS LIKE AN ADVENTURE!!
programmes.d: When Brook is overmatched by the zombie samurai, Zoro steps in to help the skeleton get his shadow back. Meanwhile, Luffy prepares for a battle with Gecko Moria, and Sanji interrupts an undead wedding!

programmes.st: BLAZING KNIGHT SANJI!! KICK DOWN THE FAKE WEDDING
programmes.d: Despite his furious attempts, Luffy struggles to land a blow against Gecko Moria, but Sanji fares much better in his passionate attempt to defeat Nami's beastly abductor!

programmes.st: A CLEAR-CLEAR HISTORY? SANJI'S STOLEN DREAM
programmes.d: Sanji takes a beating when his opponent suddenly turns invisible, Luffy finally manages to land a blow in his battle with Gecko Moria, and Usopp uses fire to ward off a zombie bear!

programmes.st: SAVE ME, HERO!! MY ENEMY IS THE IMMORTAL PRINCESS
programmes.d: After getting the stuffing beat out of him by a zombie teddy bear, Usopp summons his sharp-shooting alter ego to help him discover the secret to defeating Perona!

programmes.st: PERONA IS TERRIFIED!! USOPP AND UNTRUTHFUL SHARE THE SAME "U"
programmes.d: Usopp reaches deep into his devious bag of tricks to even the odds in his battle with Perona. Meanwhile, Luffy can't lay a finger on Gecko Moria, and a zombie is less than gentlemanly in his battle with Robin!

programmes.st: SLASHES DANCING ON THE ROOFTOP!! SHOWDOWN: ZORO VS. RYUMA
programmes.d: While Franky and Brook watch in awe, Zorro and the zombie samurai wage a sword-slinging battle the likes of which the world has never seen before!

programmes.st: CHOPPER IS FURIOUS!! HOGBACK'S EVIL MEDICAL PRACTICES
programmes.d: Chopper can no longer contain his fury over Dr. Hogback's evil treatment of his zombie slaves. Meanwhile, Luffy prepares to face the zombie who's wearing his shadow!

programmes.st: OARS ROARS! COME OUT, STRAW HAT CREW

programmes.st: LUFFY IS THE ENEMY! THE ULTIMATE ZOMBIE VS. THE STRAW HAT CREW

programmes.st: YOU'RE GOING DOWN, ABSALOM!! NAMI'S LIGHTNING ATTACK OF FRIENDSHIP!!
programmes.d: Nami wakes up just in time to find out she's about to marry a zombie, but the special occasion is interrupted by very jealous warthog!

programmes.st: KNOCK HIM DOWN!! SPECIAL ATTACK: STRAW HAT DOCKING?
programmes.d: Nami attempts to track down some missing treasure, Brook searches the kitchen for a mystery ingredient, and a heroic team effort topples Oars!

programmes.st: THE SILENT ASSAULT!! THE MYSTERIOUS VISTOR, "TYRANT" KUMA
programmes.d: Nami has a horrifying run in with Bartholomew Kuma, Perona becomes the latest lady to vanish, and Chopper, Franky, and Usopp team up to strike a blow against Oars!

programmes.st: OARS + MORIA / THE MOST HEINOUS COMBINATION OF BRAINS AND BRAWN
programmes.d: Kuma has an upsetting message for Moria, Luffy loses track of his intended target, and Zoro attempts to harness the power of a new sword during his battle with Oars!

programmes.st: THE SECRET PLAN TO TURN THE TABLES / NIGHTMARE LUFFY MAKES HIS APPEARANCE
programmes.d: Brook arrives with the salt needed to stop Oars, but the monster shows off some special new abilities. Deep in the forest, Luffy makes some new friends who help him power up!

programmes.d: Brook joins the fight as the Straw Hats valiantly try to hold off Oars and Moria until Luffy returns. Unfortunately, even their combined powers are no match for these evil enemies!

Discover the staggering blunder that caused a plane in Buenos Aires to crash on takeoff.
Behind-the-scenes of the crash, investigation, and political schemes of South African Airlines Flight 295.

Soar over Idaho and explore this state's most unexpected sites, from Hell's Canyon to breathtaking waterfalls.
An aerial tour over the world's first national park showcases Yellowstone's visual wonders, diverse wildlife, and rich history.
From Molokai to Maui, discover the stunning landscapes of Hawaii's eight major islands without ever touching the ground.
Easy Company's mission to take out German howitzers hours before the D-Day invasion.
In 1942, a secret British regiment led a daring raid on a Nazi-occupied Libyan harbor.
A countdown of the ten greatest military planes of World War II, including the Japanese Zero, the Nazi ME 109, and the B-29 Superfortress.
An inside look at Japan's A6M Zero, the most feared fighter at the start of World War II.
The Vietnam-era OV-10 Bronco is pulled out of retirement to join the fight against ISIS.
The history of the B-17 reveals how the aircraft evolved into the USAF's most lethal bomber in WWII's European and Pacific campaigns.
Linda Forney and her pet dog Cocoa Gin set off to explore one of  the seven  natural  wonders  of  the Grand  Canyon.
Jim  Davidson  and  best-friend  Mike  Price  embark  on  a  mountaineering expedition.
While climbing in the French Alps, two friends find themselves trapped on a tiny ledge in a viscous storm.
A visit from Tom's son Chad goes terribly wrong and Marty's flight back from the Revelation Mountains is delayed.
Marty is stranded in the Revelation Mountains with one last chance to get home, while Kyle and Ben launch a nighttime stakeout to stop a predator.
Tom battles a dangerous ice jam. Marty launches a last-ditch escape from the Revelations, and a deadly predator returns to the Ruby Valley.
Marty is forced to make a mid-flight detour that costs him precious fuel; Rich faces his worst fear when the dogs run off in pursuit of a deadly predator, and Kyle takes down a beast.
Relive the mountain men's best battles against nature's deadliest predators.
After surviving last year's record-breaking cold, the Mountain Men return more prepared than ever to do battle against Mother Nature.
Roger, his new girlfriend Shelly and her two young daughters are on a daytrip in the Arizona desert.
Six men are competing in a yacht race from Texas to the Gulf of Mexico, when their yacht capsizes.
50-year-old mountaineer Lincoln Hall attempted to climb Everest in 1984 but didn't reach the summit.
In 2003, David Hunt and his daughter Leia, set off on a snowmobiling adventure in the Quebec backcountry.
Two students are on a 3-day hike, but when their path is blocked by ice, the girls take a detour.
Tom defends his home against a bear threat while Morgan makes a deadly miscalculation on thin ice.
Morgan gets caught in the grips of an ice desert with no shelter in sight and Marty's return to Alaska's Revelation Mountains takes an unexpected turn.
Morgan climbs into the treacherous Alaska Range; Rich goes to war with the wolves.

Jarrett seemingly faces the seven plagues and more when he hauls a pedal pub and a side load of sod.
Jarrett's brush with Rock n' Roll fame takes a turn for the worse when he scrambles to deliver their chicken car on time.
After challenging Chris that girls can do anything a guy can, Robbie takes over a very "macho" shipment.

Team Salvage has been called in to rescue a stranded vessel stuck in a mangrove jungle in North Queensland. It got blown in there by Cyclone Debbie. The only way they can get it out is to winch it out. But there’s a problem.
Team Salvage is trying to re-float a damaged yacht. The owners want to keep it and get it repaired. The squad successfully winches it out only to discover it’s leaking and is full of toxic fumes.

Roy hires bodyguards to keep the riff-raff away at an auction in Brampton. Bogart quits, but just when he thinks he's out can Paul pull him back in? Rick and Cindy make a wicked-awesome discovery, and Ursula gets carried away.

Roy's arch-nemesis, auctioneer Patrick Pecker, calls an auction on Weston Road. While Roy seeks to lift the curse, Ursula works her charm. Meanwhile, Bogart reads Paul the riot-shirt, and Rick and Cindy get lost.

programmes.st: Who Wants To Be A Bazillionaire
programmes.d: Ursula's new employee Tania is tough, goth, and not afraid to pick fights at auctions in Toronto. Of course, Cindy isn't about to back down. When Bogart decides to assert himself, he threatens Roy's claim to the title of biggest jerk at the auction.

Part-time janitors Mike and Armando hope to clean up at an auction in Emery Village. Rick and Cindy don't want more newbies but Paul is always looking out to replace Bogart. Roy can't handle the tooth but Ursula's locker is totally tubular.

Buying partnerships are tested at an auction in Brampton. Bogart puts Paul on a diet. Meanwhile, Rick squirms when Cindy wants him to wear a spiffy new shirt. Ursula tries on her bossy-pants, but what Roy finds really puts the icing on the cake.

programmes.st: Keep Your Friends Close And The Veterans Closer
programmes.d: Paul and Bogart declare storage war on the veterans at an auction in Orillia. Roy bums a ride off them instead. Ursula has a bad hair day, and Rick and Cindy meet former Stanley Cup Champion Nick Kypreos.

Roy is up to his usual antics at an auction in the Old Weston neighborhood of Toronto but this time Ursula strikes back. Paul and Bogart are the epitome of the blind leading the blind, while Rick and Cindy's locker is more than meets the eye.

Paul and Bogart concoct an entirely new strategy for an auction in Leaside: to have no strategy at all. Rick and Cindy play doctor, Ursula gets her geek on, and Roy rocks out with Canadian metal icon Robb Reiner.

programmes.st: You Scratch My Back And I’ll Scratch Yours

Team Salvage is in the middle of a major beach rescue. But things are not looking good. Christopher the winch beast is bogged, their maintenance van is bogged and the excavator they brought in to toe Christopher out is also bogged.
The Oak Island team returns to borehole 10-X in search of new clues.
Rick Lagina travels to the Franklin D. Roosevelt library to find out why the former U.S. President was obsessed with Oak Island.
Rick and Marty decide to dig a third hole at the Money Pit after Rick finds even more evidence connecting Oak Island to the Knights Templar.
The Enterprise picks up a intergalactic conman, Harry Mudd, and three incredibly beautiful women who harbor a dark secret.

programmes.st: What Are Little Girls Made Of?
programmes.d: Nurse Christine Chapel is reunited with her old fiancé on Exo III, but the scientist has plans for Captain Kirk and the Federation.
A strange group of children are discovered on an Earth-like planet.
Kirk investigates an experimental facility for holding prisoners and finds a sinister scheme.
Kirk bluffs his way past what appears to be a powerful alien.
Spock hijacks the Enterprise to return an injured Captain Pike to Talos IV.
Spock hijacks the Enterprise to return an injured Captain Pike to Talos IV.
Kirk is one of the last survivors who can identify a mass killer, who lurks among a Shakespearean troupe aboard the Enterprise.
The Enterprise must decide on its response when a Romulan ship makes a destructively hostile armed probe of Federation territory.
A U.S.S. Enterprise landing party beams down to an uncharted planet. The planet seems like a perfect candidate for shore leave with its "Earth-type" characteristics.
Spock commands a stranded away team when their shuttlecraft is stranded on a planet with hostile natives.
A powerful entity known as Trelane torments the crew of the Enterprise.
The U.S.S. Enterprise is in pursuit of an unknown alien ship which has destroyed a Starfleet base.
The U.S.S. Enterprise is thrown into a time warp and ends up orbiting Earth in the 20th century.
Captain Kirk's career is at stake when he is put on trial for the loss of a crewman during an ion storm.
The Enterprise encounters a seemingly peaceful civilization run by a "benevolent" being named Landru...who intends for them to join his people.
Kirk meets Khan, a notorious dictator, and leader of Earth's Eugenics War.
After falling in love with a woman whose species is unable to walk in "normal" gravity, Bashir develops a technology that could free her of her wheelchair forever.
A Ferengi female, defying the law and disguising herself as a male, risks it all when she falls in love with Quark.
An attack on Quark's life brings Odo face to face with a five-year-old unsolved murder--for which Kira was a prime suspect.
Sisko falls in love for the first time since his wife's death, but the object of his affection may not be all that she seems.
Kira is torn when a displaced alien race arrives on Deep Space Nine and claims Bajor as its people's legendary homeland.
Quark feels threatened when a charming swindler arrives on Deep Space Nine and opens a competing bar.
Odo's mentor arrives on Deep Space Nine intent on resuming his search for Odo's true origin.
Bashir and O'Brien work to rid two alien races of deadly weapons, unaware that their hosts intend to sacrifice them as part of the peace process.
O'Brien returns from a security mission to notice that the entire crew has seemingly turned against him.
Sisko and O'Brien are stranded on a planet inhabited by humans who have rejected any form of technology.
Odo and Dax try to solve the mystery of an alien planet whose inhabitants are disappearing without explanation.
While hosting her first Trill initiate, Dax discovers a tiny, developing universe, which threatens to destroy the station as it expands.
When Quark is reunited with the love of his life, a Cardassian who is now a fugitive, he is ready to sacrifice everything to win her back.
Dax risks her life and her future with Starfleet to fulfill a blood oath made with three aged Klingons.
Sisko uncovers a Federation terrorist group whose actions could start another war with the Cardassians.
Sisko and Gul Dukat join forces in an effort to avert a war between the Cardassians and a group of Federation colonists led by Sisko's old friend.
Bashir fights to save his Cardassian friend Garak, who is slowly being killed by a brain implant to which he is addicted.
While dissension grows among Xindi ranks, Enterprise tries to recover from a devastating attack.
Two high-ranking Xindi offer to stop the launch of their superweapon if Archer can prove they've been manipulated. Meanwhile, the crew mourns their lost mates.
An attempt to use a Xindi subspace corridor leads the Enterprise crew to a bizarre encounter with their own descendants.
Archer and Hoshi stand before the Xindi Council as T'Pol and Reed lead a team into the heart of a Sphere.
With help from Xindi allies, the Enterprise crew attempts to stop the arming of the superweapon aimed toward Earth.
Archer puts his life on the line in a risky gambit to intercept the Xindi superweapon and disarm it from within.
Archer and the NX-01 find themselves in Earth's past, with events of World War II altered by the Temporal Cold War.
With Silik's help, Archer hones in on the temporal operative who altered Earth's past and threatens to destroy all of time.
Once the NX-01 finally returns to Earth, the weary crewmen face repercussions of their journeys, both positive and negative.
When the genetic supermen remaining from the Eugenics Wars hijack a Klingon ship, Archer must rely on their creator, the criminal Dr. Arik Soong, to help hunt them down.
Arik Soong leads his band of Augments to a medical facility where hundreds of genetically enhanced embryos are still stored, intending to retrieve them and bring them to life.
In defiance of their "father," Arik Soong's Augments devise a heinous plot against the Klingons which will surely lead to interstellar war.
Earth's embassy on Vulcan is bombed, and the ensuing investigation puts Archer and T'Pol on the trail of a Vulcan religious faction hiding in a treacherous desert.
Archer and T'Pol encounter the Syrrannites, a radical group hiding in the Vulcan desert, while the NX-01 crew contends with Vulcan power ploys.

Archer, T'Pol and T'Pau attempt to bring the Kir'Shara an artifact believed to contain Surak's original writings  to the Vulcan capital, as the NX-01 gets involved in a Vulcan-Andorian military clash.
The inventor of the transporter, Emory Erickson, comes aboard Enterprise for a risky experiment.
Noncorporeal aliens study the Enterprise crew as they respond to a fatal viral infection brought on board from an away mission.
LaForge gets left behind on a storm-plagued planet when the rest of his team encounters a Romulan warrior.
While the Enterprise hosts negotiations for control of a stable wormhole, Troi forms a personal relationship with an opposing negotiator, unaware of his true being.
The Enterprise pursues a race of "gatherers" who continue to raid Federation outposts, unaware of the dangers lurking among them.
When a Romulan officer defects to the Federation with a warning of an impending invasion, Capt. Picard struggles to decide if he is to be believed.
Investigating a planet applying for membership into the Federation, the crew of the Enterprise finds a group of inhabitants who used to be soldiers but now fight for their very existence.
While visiting a planet under civil war, Dr. Crusher is taken hostage by an opposing faction of the planet's ruling government.
Much to Picard's displeasure, Q reappears on the Enterprise, claiming to have been ejected from the Q Continuum, and therefore, lost his powers.
The widow of respected scientist Dr. Nel Apgar accuses Riker of seducing her and killing her husband. Rather than turn Riker over for unfavorable trial, the Enterprise reconstructs the facts.
The Enterprise C enters the Enterprise D's time and space continuum, where they find Picard and crew in a constant state of war with the Klingons, and only Guinan knows it.
After returning from a cybernetics conference to the Enterprise, Data creates his own "child," much to the chagrin of his captain, and without regards to the ramifications with Starfleet.
A Klingon commander boards the Enterprise in an officer exchange program initiated by Starfleet, much to the chagrin of the crew.
Picard is kidnapped and held with three different aliens and meanwhile replaced with a replica as impostor captain.

After mediating a difficult peace agreement, Captain Picard is encouraged to take a much needed rest on a vacationing planet, where he's visited by a strange race from the future, in search of a dangerous weapon.
The Enterprise reaches out to an alien being while dancing around with the Romulans, who want to attack it in an act of vengeance.
A shy member of the "Enterprise" crew becomes addicted to the holodeck, where relationships are easier there than in real life, when his knowledge is needed in engineering.
When transporting a dangerous material to the Enterprise, Data is kidnapped and the crew is led to believe he is dead when the shuttlecraft he was piloting explodes enroute.
Legendary Federation ambassador Sarek visits the Enterprise to conclude peace talks with a race called the Legarans.
A need to test herself leads Torres down a path of self-destruction.
The Voyager crew discovers an alien training ground for the destruction of Earth.
Neelix balks at telling Naomi that her mother and others have gone missing on an away mission.
Fifteen years after making a horrible mistake, Kim attempts to rewrite history.
Seven experiences the Borg version of multiple personality disorder.
Torres is forced to put her life in the hands of a mortal enemy that uses biochemical secretions to give commands.
Paris is confined to the Brig after interfering with the affairs of an alien race.
Janeway falls for a man who may be using her to take over Voyager.
Someone is trying to keep the Doctor from remembering the incidents surrounding a crewmember's death.
Janeway and Paris join forces to defeat the evil Doctor Chaotica.
Stranded on a desolate planet with a beautiful female, Tuvok struggles to ignore the emotions his Vulcan master taught him to suppress.
The crew is in serious danger when all of their dreams seem to come true and home seems closer in sight.
During a mission against the Borg, Seven of Nine is lured back to the Collective.
When Seven is threatened by assimilation into the Collective, Janeway launches an all-out mission to rescue her.
Kim puts his future with Voyager at risk when he chooses love over duty.
As crewmembers begin dying, they make a startling discovery about their true identities.
An alien race chooses to communicate with Voyager through Chakotay on the holodeck.

The team comes across a small village with a revered leader. Beckett soon becomes so enamored by his host he brings him to Atlantis. But soon, McKay discovers that Lucius is using some sort of pheromone to enchant those around him.

Exploring a village, the team is suddenly attacked and taken prisoner as Ronon had unknowingly lured the Wraith there. The villagers set Sheppard and Teyla free, who mobilize a strike force. When they return, the village has been devastated.

Dr. McKay discovers a reference to an abandoned Ancient testing site. At the site, the team discovers a vast metropolis supporting millions of Ancients. Eager to create an alliance, Weir is shocked when their leader Oberoth refuses the offer.

Waking up in a psychiatric hospital outside of D.C., Weir is shocked to discover that her entire experience in Atlantis over the last two years was all in her imagination. She learns that a car accident left her suffering from delusional psychosis.

Summoned to a planet by a communication code, the team is ambushed by Kolya, who has now created his own faction of Genii after being forced from the inner circle. While the rest of the team manages to escape, Sheppard is taken prisoner.

McKay is called back to earth to convince his estranged sister, Jeannie Miller, to assist the Air Force. McKay and Jeannie travel to Atlantis and begin the experiment which is initially successful until a McKay from the parallel universe appears.

When a military research base is attacked, a small group of civilians and military personnel escape on a ship into deep space. But divisions emerge between those who want to attempt a return to Earth and those who want to remain aboard the Destiny.

After secretly contacting Homeworld Command, Dr. Rush (Robert Carlyle) claims that he has been placed in charge by Gen. O’Neill (Richard Dean Anderson) and that there is no hope of returning to Earth. But his assertions are soon questioned.

With the air supply failing on the Destiny, a team disembarks to a desert-like planet in search of a mineral needed to scrub the ship's air of carbon dioxide. While one team presses on to find the vital mineral, the other has another goal in mind.

The crew has been working throughout the night to try and determine why the ship’s power reserves are critically low. But when Destiny’s flight path towards a solar system reveals three planets, the entire crew hopes that one of them is habitable.

When Carter and Teal'c fly to the Asgard world of Hala in hopes of finding a way to revive O'Neill, they are attacked by Replicators, who take Carter prisoner. Meanwhile, Dr. Weir and Jackson attempt to negotiate a treaty with Goa'uld System Lords.

The Goa'uld send a mothership to Earth, demanding that it prove its superior defenses. As Dr. Weir applies her most expert diplomatic tactics, Jackson and the still-unconscious body of O'Neill are unexpectedly beamed aboard Thor's ship.

When Jackson contracts a mysterious illness, O'Neill is convinced that a contagion has infected the base and orders a lockdown. But when Jackson reveals that he was actually possessed by Anubis, O'Neill must discover the identity of the new host!

O'Neill deals with a visit from the president and negotiations between two warring tribes from Amra. When SG-1 is captured, he's forced to choose between the safety of the team and the fate of a planet, making him question his competency!

On a distant planet the Stargate has become a symbol to the people, and some believe that the gods will return through it to reward the faithful. SG-1 realizes that those gods are the Goa'uld and warn of the danger they may face.

The team agrees that an easy VR simulator is a useless training tool against the Goa'uld. Teal'c lets it learn from him, but as he plays, the game sends a shock each time he dies, and if he doesn't defeat the game, the chair will kill him.

Teal'c, having finally been cleared to live off-base, settles into his new neighborhood. His neighbors love him. He's quiet and he has become a sort of protector of his community but not everybody is as pleased about Teal'c's civilian assimilation.

It’s that time of year when the berries are about to burst into bloom – and it looks like this will be a bumper crop!
The Berry Blossom Festival is underway and everyone in Strawberryland is having a Grand Time, thanks to the selfless efforts of Strawberry Shortcake.
Strawberry and her friends love to dance – and the Peculiar Purple Pieman of Porcupine Peak is taking advantage of that!
It’s winter and the pond’s frozen and that means Strawberry and friends can ice skate!
When Strawberry & her friends decide to put on a talent show, they plan to enter themselves as a band called Strawberry Jams
Strawberry and her friends are getting the band back together to perform at a local festival, but Ginger Snap is out of town.
When the girls discover that Apple's groove booties can teach the pups to dance, Plum gets an idea for a Doggie Dance Show.
When a simple tune Cherry composes goes viral on the Berryweb, Cherry quickly gets fed up with everyone listening to this song, everywhere, all the time.

Election fever grips the Addams household, as Gomez (John Astin) supports the council candidate whose campaign promise is to drain the town's disgusting bogs.  Morticia (Carolyn Jones), who likes "the lovely bogs," labels the candidate an extremist.

programmes.st: The Addams Family Goes To School
programmes.d: Morticia and Gomez decide to keep Wednesday and Pugsley home from school after Morticia sees the fairy tales they have to read.  When the truant officer comes to investigate, he is shocked at what he finds.

Morticia calls a psychiatrist after she fears Pugsley is becoming normal after he abandons his pet octopus for a puppy and is seen wearing a Boy Scout uniform, playing with a baseball bat, and helping an old lady cross the street.

Grandmama (Blossom Rock) is hauled off to jail for setting up a fortune-telling booth in the Addamses' living room.  Gomez (John Astin) volunteers to act as attorney, and the court session becomes a shambles.

programmes.st: Mother Lurch Visits The Addams Family
programmes.d: Lurch's tiny fire-eating mother visits and demands that Lurch's employers wait on her boy hand-and-foot after Lurch leads her to believe that it's his house. Lurch revels in the unexpected attention he gets from Morticia and Gomez.

Ophelia Frump is madly in love with Horatio Bartholomew, the man who has everything, except the truth about her relatives. Morticia, not convinced by Bartholomew, persuades playboy Cousin Itt to stir the embers of his past romance with Ophelia.

Uncle Fester applies for a job as an insurance salesman with the same company which is threatening to cancel the Addamses' policy (because Fester keeps blowing things up).  Fester convinces the company interviewer that he is qualified for the job.

Morticia's cousin, Melancholia, wants to marry Clarence P. Harvey after most of her marital prospects have joined the Foreign Legion. Clarence recoils when Melancholia puts on a campaign to win him, backed by Morticia, Gomez and Clarence's boss.

Wednesday and Pugsley return in tears from trick-or-treating because a neighbor has told them there is no such thing as a witch.  Morticia and Gomez plan to prove to the children that they do exist--by summoning a witch to a séance.

Lurch becomes inconsolable when Gomez donates the family antique harpsichord to a collector.  Gomez and Morticia offer Lurch a balalaika and a set of drums.  When this proves unsatisfactory, Gomez and Fester decide to build a new harpsichord.

Morticia and Gomez see Fester conferring with TV muscleman Jack LaGrann (Jack LaLanne), and think that Fester is planning a television career.  However, Uncle Fester confides to Lurch that he has to go on a secret diet and exercise.

A recording company's platter of Lurch's gravelly voice brings a screaming mob of teenage fans to the Addams house. To calm the crowd, Lurch seats himself at the harpsichord and rewards his fans with a song to end all songs.

Uncle Fester, who has become lonely, convinces Gomez and Morticia that it is time for him to find a bride. He decides to put an ad in the newspaper, looking for love. But things go awry when a door-to-door saleswoman comes by.

Morticia and Gomez find Grandfather Pegleg's treasure map and summon Captain Grimby.  They hope to charter his boat for the treasure hunt. But after meeting the Captain, Morticia is careful to keep the nature of the mission secret.

The Addams Family ignores notices that their house is to be condemned to make way for a freeway.  When sudden explosions cannot be traced to any member of the family but, instead, to city workmen, Gomez is forced to consider moving the house.

A pair of bank robbers are welcomed as Halloween trick-or-treaters by Morticia and Gomez.  The creepy atmosphere of the house, Morticia's smoldering holiday punch, and Lurch's ominous presence impel the crooks to abandon their plans.

There is a neighborhood burglar on the loose, and Morticia has reason to believe it could be Gomez.  Morticia decides to probe his subconscious mind for a key to his criminality after she and Uncle Fester discover loot hidden in the storeroom.

Pugsley and Wednesday start a row at a party when their gift of a tarantula upsets Harold, the birthday boy.  Harold's parents insist that the Addams children lack breeding and, therefore, are no longer allowed to play with their son.

Lurch suffers from unrequited love over Tiny Trivia (guest star Diane Jergens), Morticia's visiting school chum who only has eyes for show business.  The entire family decides to try to turn their stolid butler into a new personality.

Grandma Frump (guest star Margaret Hamilton), comes to the mistaken conclusion that her daughter, Morticia (Carolyn Jones), and Gomez (John Astin) plan to pack her off to an old folks home.  Actually, they plan to send her to a beauty farm.

When Morticia hears the stock market has crashed, she assumes that Gomez has been financially wiped out and rallies the family to help make money. Morticia gives lessons, Lurch and Fester run an escort service, and the kids run a poison drink stand.

In need of artistic fulfillment, Morticia takes up sculpting. An art critic views her first endeavor--a three-eyed Gomez statue--and clubs it with his cane. Gomez, who won't have Morticia's heart broken gets a seedy art dealer to buy it.

Pugsley copies one of his dad's old love letters and sends it to his teacher. Miss Dunbar comes to visit the Addams home and confesses to Gomez that no man has ever fallen so in love with her, leading Morticia to pretend to be the jealous wife.

Grandmama's paintings leave an art critic speechless, so Gomez sends for his friend, Sam Picasso, to teach Grandmama to paint in the abstract.  The starving artist ignores Grandmama's and Morticia's work as he eats and paints.

programmes.st: New Neighbors Meet The Addams Family
programmes.d: Newlyweds move in next door. But the honeymoon loses its tranquility when Uncle Fester enters their house through a tunnel and they flee in terror at the sight of Lurch, Grandmama sharpening her ax, and Morticia and Gomez bathing the octopus.

After Pugsley befriends Gorgo, a circus gorilla, Gorgo decides to follow Pugsley and Gomez home, where is accepted as one of the family. But Gorgo gives Morticia's tea guests, the Ladies League members, quite a shock.

Romance seems close for Thing, the Addams right-hand-in-a-box, when Gomez's aunt arrives for a visit accompanied by Lady Fingers, her handmaiden.  Thing enjoys the visit most because it gives him a chance to hold hands with one of his own kind.

Morticia's concern that Lurch is overworked leads Gomez to the operating table to assemble a custom-built secondary butler.  Lurch lets the robot do all the work and then begins to feel that he isn't needed anymore.

Determined to correct the dreadful literature that Wednesday and Pugsley are exposed to, Morticia sets out to create a new literary world. Gomez fears that his wife's first manuscript is so good, that once the publisher reads it he will lose her.

Gomez plays host to Don Xavier Molines, a family friend during his childhood in Spain, and his daughter Consuella.  Morticia's hospitality is put to the test when Consuella reveals that she has been promised in marriage to Gomez since childhood.

Morticia and Gomez visit Mayor Henson to complain that their property tax is ridiculously low. After the Mayor proves his incompetence by offering a refund, Gomez is persuaded to become a candidate for the office.

Gomez (John Astin) loses his memory after hitting his head; he fails to recognize Morticia (Carolyn Jones) and says the house looks like a condemned museum.  The Addamses take turns hitting Gomez on the head trying to help him regain his memory.

The family would like to vacation on the moon, but the billion-dollar travel cost is slightly prohibitive. Uncle Fester volunteers $21.13 and Morticia, using Gomez's new supercomputer, suggests placing a $2,000 bet on the daily double horse race.

Lucas helps his former Army captain, now an undercover federal agent, infiltrate a gang of bank robbers.

An ex-convict is blamed for a brutal crime despite his claims of rehabilitation.

A former army captain comes to North Fork to kill the man who shot down his son in a gunfight - Lucas McCain.

The girls flip over a handsome Englishman who moves in next door, but Jack and Furley become convinced that he is one of London's most sought after criminals.

To avoid a woman's angry boyfriend, Jack joins his roommates for a weekend on a farm owned by Cindy's Aunt Becky.

On September 20th, 1972 Muhammad Ali faced Floyd Patterson for a second time at Madison Square Garden in New York that ended in the seventh round due to swelling and cuts on Pattersons eye giving the victory to Ali.

On October 1st, 1975, Muhammad Ali and Joe Frazier fought for the third time for the World Heavyweight Title. Known as the "Thrilla in Manila," Ali ultimately emerged as the victor in what is considered one of the greatest boxing matches of all time.
On April 1st, 1972 Muhammad Ali and Mac Foster fought in a fifteen round bout that ended in a unanimous decision win for Ali.

programmes.t: Muhammad Ali vs Oscar Natalio Bonavena
programmes.d: On December 7th, 1970 Muhammad Ali faced Oscar Natalio Bonavena in a 15 round bout with Bonavena going down three times in the last round forcing an automatic stoggage giving the win to Ali.

On January 28th, 1974 Muhammad Ali and Joe Frazier face eachother for a second time at Madison Square Garden in New York for North American Boxing Federation Heavyweight titles resulting in a strong win for Ali.

On September 10th, 1973 Muhammad Ali and Ken Norton participated in their second meeting at the Forum in Inglewood, CA. They fought for the North American Boxing Federation Heavyweight title with Ali winning this time with split decision.
On October 31st, 2020 Naoya Inoue faced Jason Moloney in The Bubble at the MGM Grand in Las Vegas for the IBF and WBA World Super Bantamweight titles ending in a knockout in the 7th round by Inoue.

programmes.t: Naoya Inoue vs Nonito Donaire II
programmes.d: On June 7th, 2022 Naoya Inoue battled Nonoito Donaire for a second time at the Super Arena in Saitama for IBF, WBA and WBC World Bantamweight title with Inoue ending the bout in the second round defeating Donaire.

On December 15th, 2012 Nonito Donaire faced Jorge Arce at the Toyota Center in Houston, Tx. With the bout ending in the third round with a win by Donaire, Arce announced his retirement in the ring after the bout.

programmes.t: Orlando Salido vs Juan Manuel Lopez 2
programmes.d: On March 10th, 2012, Orlando Salido fought Juan Manuel Lopez for the WBO World Featherweight Title in San Juan, Puerto Rico. In a very entertaining fight with both fighters scoring knockdowns, Salido stopped Lopez in the 10th round.

programmes.t: Oscar De La Hoya vs Curtis Strong
programmes.d: On February 6th, 1993 Oscar De La Hoya and Curtis Strong fought at the Sports Arena in San Diego, Ca. in a 6 round bout that lasted 4 rounds ending in a technical knockout victory for De La Hoya.

programmes.t: Oscar De La Hoya vs Felix Sturm
programmes.d: On June 5th, 2004 Oscar De La Hoya fought Felix Sturm at the MGM Grand in Las Vegas for the WBO Middleweight title in a 12 round bout resulting in an unanimous decision win for De La Hoya.

programmes.t: Oscar De La Hoya vs Fernado Vargas
programmes.d: On September 14th, 2002, Oscar De La Hoya and Fernando Vargas fought for Super Welterweight titles at the Mandalay Bay in Las Vegas. In an incredible battle, De La Hoya was able to stop Vargas in the 11th round.

programmes.t: Oscar De La Hoya vs Giorgio Campanella

programmes.t: Oscar De La Hoya vs Hector Camacho
programmes.d: On September 13th, 1997 Oscar De La Hoya fought Hector Camacho for the WBC World Welterweight title at the Thomas and Mack Center in Las Vegas the twelve round bout ended in a unanimous decision victory for De La Hoya.

programmes.t: Oscar De La Hoya vs Jeff Mayweather
programmes.d: On March 13th, 1993 Oscar De La Hoya and Jeff Mayweather faced eachother at the Hilton Hotel in Las Vegas in an 8 round bout then ended by technical knockout in the fourth round securing the victory for De la Hoya.

programmes.d: On February 18th, 1995 Oscar De La Hoya fought John John Molina for the WBO World Lightweight title at the MGM Grand in Las Vegas in a 12 round bout resulting in a win for De La Hoya.

programmes.t: Oscar De La Hoya vs Julio Cesar Chavez 1
programmes.d: On June 7th, 1996 Oscar De La Hoya and Julio Cesar Chavez fought for the first time for WBC World super Lightweight titles at Caesars Palace in Las Vegas that ended by technical knockout in the fourth round giving the win to De La Hoya.

programmes.d: On May 3rd, 2003 Oscar De La Hoya faced Luis Ramon Campas for WBA and WBC World super welterweight title at the Mandalay Bay Resort in Las Vegas the ended by technical knockout in the 7th round with De La Hoya securing the victory.

programmes.d: On April 12th, 1997, Oscar De La Hoya fought Pernell Whitaker for the WBC Welterweight Title at Thomas & Mack Center in Las Vegas. De La Hoya won by a very controversial decision in a fight that many thought Whitaker had the superior performance.

After Si has started moonlighting as a grocery bagger, the guys show up at the store and their teasing inadvertently causes Si to lose his job and his chance to enter a local bagging competition.

Willie accompanies Kay to a local bingo tournament and gets seduced by the game, eventually embarrassing himself and Kay with his enthusiasm.
Willie takes Sadie on a tour of a local college in hopes of convincing her to stay nearby after her impending high school graduation.

When the Robertson brothers debate which of their wives makes the best cornbread, it escalates into a full-on cornbread cook-off. Meanwhile, when Jep, Martin, and Godwin play a practical joke on Uncle Si, it ends up being Si who has the last laugh.

Josh rides into a town looking for a man who asked him to come there for a job that pays $500.

A man who left Paladin to die in his place writes to Paladin and asks for his  help.
A diptheria scare slows the return of Paladin's prisoner to justice.
A desert town hires Paladin to deal with three brothers who have been poisoning the municipal water supply.
Paladin is accused of stealing a painting in the small town of Bonanza.

While General Crook and Geronimo are negotiating a treaty, a fanatic bravely challenges Geronimo's leadership and starts a series of bloody massacres in the territory. Hollister (Pat Conway) must devise a trap for the renegade to save Tombstone.

Against a background of sudden death and romance, Hollister comes to grips with beautiful young widow Sarah Curtice and her band of gunmen. Clay's efforts to combat their expanding crime wave provoke a dramatic showdown with Sarah's hired guns.

A cattle broker who deals with rustlers sets out to crush The Epitaph and Sheriff Clay Hollister, whose combined efforts are hurting his operations. He hires a has-been newspaperman to start a rival newspaper and the strategy seems to be succeeding!

Hollister stops gunman Jess Buckhorn from shooting Little Hawk (Leonard Nimoy) who denies stealing horses from a mission. Attorney Fred Griffin, the gunman's secret employer, is plotting to discredit the Indians so he can gain title to their land.

It's Sheriff Clay Hollister's duty to hang murderer Sam Edwards. However, on a fateful morning, his brother appears, armed with a case of dynamite. Saving Sam from the gallows, his brother abducts Editor Harris Claibourne to hold him hostage.

In self-defense, Sheriff Hollister gunned down the son of the richest rancher in the territory, who offers a reward for Clay's death. A Marshal of a neighboring town lures the sheriff out of town so he, himself, can kill Clay and claim the reward.
Paladin wins part of a treasure map in a poker game and goes in search of the treasure with three other men.
Two ornery old gold miners, who hate each other, have struck it rich. Problem is they talk too much, and now it appears someone is trying to kill them.
Paladin is asked by the wife of a man who is condemned to die to visit him in prison and see if new evidence can be found to clear her husband.

Jonny is forced to question how Tyla feels for him. Things are on the up for Jamie and Camilla. A new bombshell enters the villa. A shock recoupling is announced.
Catch up on an eventful fifth week in the villa, with plenty of unseen action and all the best moments crammed into one jam-packed hour.
As Tyla and Jonny look to be falling out, Theo and Jonny make up - but for how long? Are Chris and Olivia as solid as it seems? Camilla and Jamie get closer.
The islanders enjoy a day of celebrations for Camilla's birthday. Are Chris and Olivia on a break or not? Tensions continue to rise between Jonny, Theo and Tyla.
Tyla and Jonny hit the rocks, while things heat up between Camilla and Jamie. A new rap trio is formed. Emotions run high as a shock dumping is announced.
Theo makes amends after causing a scene at Jonny's departure. Chris and Olivia hit the rocks again. Alex and Montana get closer, but will they make it official?
Two familiar faces return to the villa, leaving single girls Olivia, Georgia and Tyla wondering who fancies whom. Later, the boys get the girls' hearts racing in a striptease challenge.
Mike and Sam make their moves on Tyla and Georgia. Later, a recoupling is announced, meaning one lad will be going home before the night is over.

Marty wraps up trapping season with a record haul of fur; Morgan flies solo for the first time over the towering peaks of the Great Alaska Range.
As winter closes in, Morgan and Margaret fly North to track down the great caribou migration and secure meat; Marty preps his trapline for the arrival of his daughter, Noah.

On one of the coldest frontiers on the planet, the Ice Road Truckers brave treacherous terrain to deliver crucial supplies to northern diamond mines. Take a look back at the highs and lows of the first season.
It is a job only a few would dare. This year, four ice road truckers, Hugh, Alex, Rick, and Drew, return from last season to join Arctic veterans as they venture 200 miles north of the Arctic Circle.

After just two days in the Arctic, the critical demands of the oil exploration sites are testing the limits of the truckers and their machines. Both the veterans and rookies are delayed in the shop by mechanical failures.

Just five days into the Arctic adventure, Mother Nature is about to strike and wreak havoc on the ice roads. Making matters worse is a report of a trucker who has run off the road and is stranded on the weakest part.
As the logging season winds down, the pressure to produce, heats up. In Alaska, a family emergency takes Mark from the yarder seat and with no time for a shut down.
It's time to finish the season strong. In Florida, the Log-Off is locked in a dead heat, and with Joe and Swilley sidelined.
It's a battle for survival in logging country. In Bayou country, Shelby's nighttime mission brings him face-to-face with an alligator.
Logging country is turned upside down when one of the mountain's best bows out. At Papac Alaska, the men suffer under the reign of a new yarder operator.
Rich's cougar hunt takes a dark turn in Montana. Marty competes with a wolf pack for food. Tom and Will race an oncoming storm that puts them in jeopardy.
Charlie spends the night injured and alone in Maine. In Montana Tom investigates signs of a predator lurking too close to home.
Tom struggles to keep a deadly wolf pack off his land despite an injury. Rich tracks a large buck over tough terrain on his mid-winter hunting trip.
In Alaska, Marty tries to capitalize on his recent string of good luck by building a second cabin at the far end of his trap line.

Despite his worst start ever, The King of the Swamp is determined to fill his 500-plus tags this year. Armed with the help of fellow swamper Daniel Edgar's family, he takes on the high water and cold weather in true Cajun fashion.
Despite help from The Edgar family, The King of the Swamp, Troy Landry is still behind on his tag count.
Willie Edwards is back and this year he's striking out on his own. Armed with his trademark treble hook, this solo hunter is blind-sided by the biggest monster he's ever taken on.
After a group activity falls apart Tori and Beck decide to go on an "Opposite Date" where they do things that people would never do on a REAL date.
Sikowitz challenges the kids to go a week without using their phones, laptops, or other portable electronic devices. The kids accept and quickly realize it's not going to be as easy as they thought.

programmes.t: Victorious: Three Girls And A Moose
programmes.d: Tori, Cat, and Jade compete with each other to win the affection of Beck's big, handsome, hockey-loving Canadian friend, Moose.
Beck wants to ask a girl out but is worried about Jade's reaction, so Tori and Andre attempt to get Jade a date to even the playing field. Robbie works to remove a butterfly stuck in Cat's ear.
Mason Thornesmith's bratty 12-year-old kid wants to buy Rex from Robbie.  Meanwhile, a masked flour thrower is on the loose in Hollywood Arts.

Andre stays with Tori to work on a song for class.  They quickly find they aren't the best roommates.  Jade discovers an unflattering picture of herself on the internet, and conspires to take it down.
Sikowitz challenges the students to say yes to everything for one week.  The gang agrees, and they soon find themselves out of their respective comfort zones.
Tori is selected to be the team captain for a new game show, Brain Squeezers. She has to choose 3 teammates to compete with her and quickly becomes overwhelmed by requests from the gang.
When Tori gets invited to sing the national anthem at a televised basketball game, she worries she'll forget the lyrics, but ends up in a much more embarrassing encounter with the team's mascot.

Andre gets Tori a job at a frozen yogurt stand, but work may keep them from performing at the Hollywood Arts Cowboy Luau.  Robbie wants to ask Cat to the luau, but asks someone else, making Cat jealous.
Tori and the gang compete to see who can get the most followers on The Slap.  But when they get caught up in the competition, they neglect their schoolwork and their friendships.
Tori wins a contest to sing the opening number at a big music awards show, but the producer wants to totally change her look and behavior. Tori agrees, but finds that she doesn't like her new image.

After Tori fills in for her ailing sister in a big musical showcase, Tori is asked to enroll at an elite performing arts high school.  But once there, Tori struggles to fit in to her new surroundings.
Tori goes all out to master an iconic Hollywood Arts monologue in Sikowitz's class.  Meanwhile, André and Robbie join a ballet class to meet girls, with disastrous results.
Tori has to defend herself after Jade claims Tori hurt her in a stage fighting exercise.  Meanwhile, Trina has to fend off Robbie's advances when he thinks their stage kiss meant something.
Tori accidentally gets Beck fired from a small role in a movie, then must figure out a way to get him his job back.  Meanwhile, Robbie suffers frightening nightmares about his best friend Rex.
Tori gets the lead in a high profile school musical, but freaks out when a stage makeup project goes awry, and she's left looking like a zombie on opening night.
After a jealous Jade dumps Beck, she soon regrets it and recruits Tori to help get him back.  Meanwhile, Trina puts on a one-woman show and tells Robbie he better give it a good review… or else!
Tori struggles to find the perfect birthday gift for Trina, then decides to write her sister a song as a present.  An ungrateful Trina turns the song into cash by selling it, enraging Tori.

Tori suggests Robbie capture videos of students' everyday lives to increase his blog traffic, but when the camera is turned on Tori, she asks him to stop.  Only Robbie doesn't and Tori realizes she's created a monster.

programmes.t: Victorious: A Film by Dale Squires
programmes.d: When a hot young filmmaker comes to Hollywood Arts, the kids are excited to work on his project.  But when the film is released, and they aren't given credit, the kids turn to revenge.
As the kids prepare for a big play, Rex is accidentally sucked into a giant fan and Tori is responsible.  Robbie is an emotional wreck, and it's up to Tori to save the day by saving Rex's life.
Sikowitz recruits the gang to form a children's band for a friend's party.  When a leaked video of the group's performance becomes popular, Andre struggles to be taken seriously as a musician.

Cat begins dating Tori's ex-boyfriend, Danny (Matt Angel) and Tori becomes jealous. Meanwhile, Trina convinces Robbie, Andre, Jade and Beck to indulge their feet in callus-eating fish that she's been buying from some stranger.
Sikowitz invites the gang to have a sleepover at his house in order to teach them a lesson in method acting.
The kids are excited to hear that they'll be the stars of a new reality show being filmed at Hollywood Arts. Meanwhile, Trina and Robbie are forced to work at The Grub Truck after injuring Festus.
Tori discovers that her friends have been secretly going to a fancy restaurant instead of playing in an annual ping pong tournament.
Tori agrees to help Jade find a theater to perform a play Jade wrote. But when the sponsor demands changes that will ruin Jade's play, Tori has to make things right before opening night.

A heat wave hits LA and the gang heads for the beach in Beck's RV. But once there, they find themselves trapped inside the RV as the temperature rises. Oblivious, Cat parties it up with some cute boys.
Tori's flight home is delayed, leaving her no time to finish a school project with her friends. She attempts to get the work done with them over video chat, but things keep getting in the way.

Tori's friends sing at a local karaoke club and end up competing with a pair of stuck-up girls who are regular performers there. Competing with those girls proves to be more difficult than they expect, since one of the girls' father owns the club.
Tori auditions for a role in a movie. But after exaggerating on her resume, she gets hired as a stunt double. When Tori finds out her stunt is falling off a building, she's not sure she can do it.
When Principal Eikner leaves Hollywood Arts, the school hires a new principal who makes all the students re-audition in order to keep their spots. Who will get kicked out?

The story of how scientists solved a 1992 murder case involving cremation. It takes a long time and a fire to cremate a human body and destroy evidence of foul play. But the coroner who performed the autopsy on the body found telltale clues.

The investigation into a brutal attack on two boys near a pond relied on evidence fished out of the murky water. It was the first case where diatom evidence was used to place a suspect at the scene of the crime.

A look back at the case of the "River Park Rapist," who assaulted four women in South Bend, Indiana, in 1996. Law enforcement officers arrested Richard Alexander, who was convicted in 1998 and sentenced to 70 years in prison.

The 1996 Seattle murder of suburban couple Raquel Rivera and Jay Johnson is detailed. Evidence from the couple's dog, Chief, eventually ties one of the murderers to the scene. This is one of the first cases where dog DNA was used to convict.

The disappearance of Philadelphia college athlete Aimee Willard is investigated after her car was found on the roadside. When her body is found, the police find unusual marks on her body and DNA evidence that eventually leads to her killer.
The apparent overdose suicide of Reverend Bill Guthrie's wife, Sharon, is investigated, and detectives recover incriminating files from Bill's computer and learn of his infidelity.

The murders of an elderly couple leave police stumped until, two years later, they receive a major break. A jeweler looking through old newspaper clippings recognizes a necklace the female victim wore as having been pawned in her own shop.
The murder of 9-year-old Jessica Knott is investigated. Investigators use a garbage bag to connect suspect James Edward Crow Jr. to the crime.
A woman disappeared along a California highway in 1991. Three years later, the case was solved when a man's refrigerated truck was looked upon with suspicion.
A woman was shot to death. But was it a homicide or a suicide? It would take the expertise of forensic experts and two jury trials to determine the fate of the accused killer.

An examination of the first time animal DNA was used to solve a criminal case. When the body of Douglas Beamish's estranged wife, Shirley Duguay, was discovered, authorities linked 20 cat hairs found on her jacket to a cat owned by Beamish's parents.

The founder of American Atheists disappeared in 1995 along with one of her sons, a granddaughter, and $500,000 in gold coins. The police homed in on several suspects, including David R. Waters, who worked for American Atheists.
Doctors cannot pinpoint the source of a businessman's illness.
The story of the 1984 Rajneeshee bioterror attack. Investigators uncover a plot to overthrow the government after a unique strain of Salmonella makes people ill.
A child's father was suspected when she was killed, but years later, police learned a convicted murderer lived nearby. Tiny drops of blood helped police solve the crime.
A murder investigation is helped by a legal requirement that bars have video cameras installed on the premises. Video, hair, and blood lead to the murderer.
Two eyewitnesses may hold the key to the death of a motorcycle gang member.
A murder investigation is stymied by the lack of a body, but police find a few charred remains, including a tooth whose filling contains properties that help investigators identify the corpse.

1995-1997-A series of unsolved kidnappings and sexual assaults occur in California. A victim says that she left something behind in the assailants vehicle which may send investigators in the right direction.
In Pennsylvania, a passerby finds the torso of a woman in a cardboard box. Investigators rely on insect activity analysis by a forensic entomologist to determine when the murder victim was killed.

The police investigate when a severed leg is discovered in the garbage. Conventional means of identifying the victim are impossible, leading investigators to rely on DNA, forensic anthropology, and toxicology to identify the victim.
A serial arsonist starts several fires that cause millions of dollars worth of damage and the deaths of three people. He is discovered partly through the use of forensic hypnosis.
When the mail-order bride of a former army sergeant goes missing, investigators look into the deaths of the man's previous two wives.

The wife of a murdered horse rancher explains that the last time she saw her husband was when he was leaving the house to go jogging. Police become suspicious when forensic evidence eventually leads investigators back to the ranch.
In 2002, the eyes of the world were on Virginia and Maryland. A serial sniper was on the loose, killing innocent, unsuspecting citizens. Just how was he caught?

Sheila Bryan, who was convicted of killing her mother in a car fire, is granted a new trial. A fire expert witness's opinion on how the fire ignited differs from the prosecution's theory. If verified, it would clear Bryan of any culpability.
Computers aid the police and FBI in solving a string of crimes in St. Louis.

The story of firefighter Michelle Baker is related. After meeting Dr. Maynard Muntzing, she became pregnant with him. After this news, she was ill whenever they were together. The coincidences led her to suspect that he was doing her harm.

A look back at a trio of unsolved murders that occurred in Wichita Falls, Texas, during the 1980s details how a fourth murder from the same time period provided the police with more than they realized.
Phone mapping, wiretapping and other forensic evidence help to solve a complicated crime.

Janet Overton died suspiciously in 1988, and the investigation hit a dead end when the autopsy indicated no foul play was involved. A telephone tip and the sensitive nose of a forensic examiner indicated otherwise.

In 1981, an 86-year-old California woman was murdered, and her house was ransacked. The crime would remain unsolved for sixteen years, until DNA profiling and new fingerprint technology helped identify the killer.

Forensic scientists work with the only clue recovered from a multiple-victim shooting: a 12-gauge shotgun. Scientists use unique methods to lift the serial number from the weapon to trace it to its owner.
Detectives use a forged signature to find a woman's abductor.
In the case of the Center City Rapist and the murder of Shannon Schieber, Philadelphia authorities use an anonymous letter and geographic profiling to hone in on a suspect.
In 1993, worldwide attention focused on a rash of robberies that targeted tourists in Florida.
Technology able to analyze human bite-marks yields information on a woman's death.
A nurse learns that she has been deliberately infected with HIV.

In 1999, a 12-year-old was found murdered in her home, and it changed the feeling of security residents had in the small town of Waseca, Minnesota. Despite a meticulous search of the home and an exhaustive investigation, police had no suspects.
In 1962, the people of the small town of Hanford, California, lost their sense of peace when one of their own, 15-year-old Marlene Miller, was murdered.

In 1993, the state of Florida was known for more than just Disney World. Worldwide attention focused on a rash of robberies that targeted tourists. Some vacationers were killed in these attacks, but some fought and survived despite severe injuries.

A woman is shot to death in her store just one day before she is to testify against the man accused of robbing her. The robber becomes the prime suspect, but he has a solid alibi: a time-stamped videotape of his activities on the day of the murder.
At a murder scene, investigators find a shoe print, several foreign hairs, and unknown fingerprints. But they believe the most telling piece of evidence is the bite mark on the victim's chest.

A woman's death in Pennsylvania triggers a homicide investigation into another woman's death in North Carolina. The similarities in the cases were striking, and examiners must determine if the suspect's story about accidental drowning is all wet.

A 34-year-old nurse experiences a variety of flu-like symptoms. None of her doctors can discover the cause until she visits the gynecologist for a routine checkup. Then she learns it's something far worse than the flu.

Time of death becomes pivotal after a pregnant woman is found murdered in her air-conditioned bedroom. A striking similarity between her death and an HBO movie gives examiners the clues they need to thaw out the alibi of a cold-blooded killer.
Police were puzzled by an obscure print found at a crime scene where one man had been killed, and two teenage girls were seriously injured. Neither of the girls could identify their attacker.

A man is found dead in his home, and his ex-wife has a perfect alibi. To determine the time of death, investigators need to know when the victim ate his last meal. An endocrinologist, a forensic botanist, and a short-order cook answer their question.

A man tells police he shot an intruder who had attacked and murdered his wife. The husband paints a tragic picture and is dubbed a hero. Four years later, forensic evidence leads police to reexamine the motives of this so-called hero.
A police officer accused of killing his estranged wife insists she committed suicide. Investigators say it was murder and that it was physically impossible for the woman to have shot herself.

When firefighters found an entire family dead inside their home, it looked like a murder-suicide, but there were several inconsistent clues in the rubble. Could ballistics, a time card, and some secret audiotapes unravel the mystery?

Two men were murdered while sleeping in their beds. The next night, arson destroyed a family planning clinic. Investigators wonder whether some shards of glass, paint chips, and a chicken feather could link what appeared to be two separate crimes.

A young TV news producer is raped and murdered in her apartment. Police identify two suspects, but both are cleared of any wrongdoing. The case stalls for more than a year, and then investigators turn to the Commonwealth of Virginia's DNA data bank.

With no forensic evidence inside a murder scene, investigators were baffled. But they suspected that the victim's dog had witnessed the crime. If she had, forensic scientists would have had to find a way to find out what the dog had seen.
Police are dispatched to the scene of a shooting and discover the victim's husband is one of their own: a homicide detective who says his wife accidentally shot herself in the head.

A woman was found dead in a ravine, but crucial crime scene evidence had been washed away by severe thunderstorms. Twice, the trail turned cold. Almost 20 years later, an old hat and a chip of stainless steel brought the killer to justice.

When an 11-year-old girl disappeared from a small town in a remote area of Alaska, investigators wondered if she'd been attacked by a bear or become lost in the dense woods. It turned out neither was true.

Just weeks before a witness is to testify against the man accused of sexually assaulting her, she is murdered in the front yard of her own home. Investigators immediately suspect her attacker, but they don't have enough evidence to prove his guilt.
For six years, a serial killer prowled the streets of New York City. He wrote letters to the police and the New York Post, indicating he would kill twelve people, one for each astrological sign.

A healthy young man dies mysteriously in his sleep, and toxicology tests reveal a lethal dose of lidocaine in his blood. Investigators find a suicide note and presume he killed himself until a forensic linguist examines the note.

In the summer of 1986, Kathleen Lipscomb's body was found on a deserted road outside of San Antonio. Months passed, then years, and the crime was never solved. Then Kathleen's family hired a private investigator, who discovered her diary.
The decomposed body of a young woman was discovered in a Bakersfield irrigation canal. If there was trace evidence, it had been washed away.

When a woman disappeared without a trace, there were two possible explanations: kidnapping or murder. Careful investigation, a forensic artist, and DNA profiling enabled police to find a single suspect, who was known to prey upon vulnerable women.

The investigation of the kidnapping of a prominent banker's wife led police on a wild goose chase. An unexpected discovery made by an entomologist led to a new suspect and the realization that ordinary office equipment can leave extraordinary clues.

(1/4) The TARDIS is drawn into an empty void, but they are not the only ones trapped there.
(2/4) When Rorvik learns that Romana is a time sensitive, he takes her prisoner.
(3/4) As the void shrinks, Rorvik plans to take desperate measures to escape via the mirror.
(4/4) Rorvik ignores the Doctor's warnings and takes a gamble which may have fatal consequences.
(1/4) The Keeper of Traken appears in the TARDIS seeking the Doctor's help.
(2/4) The Traken Consul hold Adric and the Doctor under sentence of death.
(3/4) Kassia, now the willing servant of the Melkur, is to become the new Keeper of Traken.
(4/4) Kassia completes the transition. The Melkur is only a shell, the real power lies within.
(1/4) To repair the TARDIS's chameleon circuit, the Doctor goes to Earth for a real police box.
(2/4) The Doctor travels to Logopolis where a series of fateful events are set in motion.
(3/4) The Master is loose on Logopolis and is determined to learn the planet's secret.
(4/4) With the fate of the universe at stake, the Doctor and the Master must collaborate.
(1/4) The arrival of the TARDIS is observed by three Urbankans.
(2/4) A Grecian philosopher reveals a bizarre secret about Monarch.
(3/4) Tegan accidentally pilots the TARDS into space, while Lin Fitu betrays the Doctor.
(4/4) The Doctor undertakes a dangerous spacewalk to rescue Tegan.
(1/4) 17th century England is being stalked by a robotic death-like figure.
(2/4) The Terileptil leader is planning to wipe out mankind with plague rats.
(3/4) A mesmerized Tegan prepares to unleash the rats on the Doctor and Richard Mace.
(4/4) Heading to London Town, the Doctor discovers more Terileptil criminals in hiding.
(1/4) On Deva Loka, Tegan falls asleep in the forest watched by the Kinda.
(2/4) When Hindle's breakdown begins, the Doctor and Todd are in danger.
(3/4) Panna shows the Doctor what the past, present and future holds for Deva Loka.

On their 17th birthday, Emma's ideal life is about to come to an end as a vengeful Sutton makes her way back to Phoenix to get her life back.
It's been a tough night for Emma and Ethan, and things get tougher when they find Sutton has disappeared after their argument. Char's aunt (CHARISMA CARPENTER) returns to town.
As an anonymous threat hangs over her head, Emma takes an opportunity to leave town and visit her dad's alma mater. Rebecca (CHARISMA CARPENTER) tries to help Char.
As Emma, Ethan and Thayer (CHRISTIAN ALEXANDER) seek the truth of what happened to Sutton at the lake, they follow a lead that raises more questions than it answers.
Emma and Ethan's loyalty to each other is strong, but the lies start to take their toll. Laurel and Ted are shocked to discover the motive behind Justin's (RANDY WAYNE) actions.
Trying to help Emma, Ethan heads into a situation that gets out of control. Mads sneaks off to see Ryan (MISHA CROSBY), and Laurel continues to see Justin (RANDY WAYNE).
When Ethan's implicated in a serious crime, he and Sutton hide out with his father, Ben Whitehorse (GIL BIRMINGHAM - The Twilight Saga), on the reservation where he grew up.
Determined to prove Ethan's innocence, Emma takes matters into her own hands, with the help of Mads and Thayer (CHRISTIAN ALEXANDER).
Arrested on murder charges, Ethan sits in jail as his friends search to prove his innocence. Dan (TYLER CHRISTOPHER) reaches out to an ex-girlfriend who is now a defense attorney.
Thayer (CHRISTIAN ALEXANDER) starts to doubt Alec's (ADRIAN PASDAR) alibi and begins investigating Rebecca's (CHARISMA CARPENTER) past. Meanwhile, Ethan is avoiding Emma.
In the explosive season finale, Sutton encourages Emma to show Kristin what they found in Rebecca's (CHARISMA CARPENTER) house, and Ethan makes a discovery that changes the game.
In the season premiere, Alec (ADRIAN PASDAR) is in jail after his arrest for murder, but he still manages to unnerve Emma. Rebecca and Sutton formulate plans for the Mercer family.
Sutton steps up her plans to win back Ethan. Feeling left out of Emma and Thayer's (CHRISTIAN ALEXANDER) growing closeness, Mads shocks Emma with a family revelation.
Sutton decides she wants her life back in order to spend more time with Ethan, and Laurel asks Jordan (recurring guest star RYAN ROTTMAN) out on a very awkward date.
Rebecca uses Sutton to further her agenda, and Emma learns that Sutton may not have told her the whole story about the night her car went in the lake.
Laurel begins asking questions about Sutton's radical personality changes and Emma renews her search for her birth mother.
The school formal creates new opportunities for secrets and lies to be revealed when everyone ends up with the wrong partner. Emma turns to Ethan for help.
Emma struggles to make sense of newfound revelations and shifts in her relationships with Ethan and Thayer (CHRISTIAN ALEXANDER). Sutton and Rebecca's bond may start to crack.
Everyone gathers to celebrate the wedding of Dan (TYLER CHRISTOPHER) and Theresa (YARA MARTINEZ), but the celebration does not go off as planned. Ethan confronts Emma.
Ethan's confession to Dan (TYLER CHRISTOPHER) threatens their relationship. Sutton gets a phone call that may provide valuable information. Emma's feelings for Thayer are tested.
In the season finale, growing suspicions have everyone on edge. Dan (TYLER CHRISTOPHER) gives Ethan an ultimatum with heartbreaking consequences and Emma finally confronts Rebecca.

In New York, the FBI and local police join forces to battle the constant influx of Colombian cocaine into the city's ports.  One detective goes undercover, posing as a Mafia wise-guy, and infiltrates a drug gang connected to Pablo Escobar's Medellin cartel.  The detective must be bold, but cautious, taking on the role of a tough-guy, but always aware that if the gang suspects anything, they won't hesitate to kill him.

In Puerto Rico, the death of a government witness, and the suspicious circumstances surrounding it, lead the FBI and local authorities to suspect corruption in the highest levels of the police force. With the help of a cooperating witness, investigators find the scope of the corruption is far greater that they first thought. Authorities struggle to capture the rouge officers, men who once swore to uphold the law, but now use their power to commit heinous crimes.

In the early 90s, a gang based in the U.S. Virgin Islands began smuggling thousands of kilos of cocaine into mainland America. Police and federal agents target the gang, but its leader remains a mystery. In an investigation spanning from Georgia to South America,  local police, the DEA, U.S. Customs and the FBI  work together to take down this dangerous drug gang.

At 9:30 am on the morning of January 30, 1997, Richmond, VA police respond to a report of shots fired at a local bank.  Two masked men brandishing automatic weapons confront, and open fire on officers responding to the call.  The gunmen exit the bank, and retreat on foot, eventually eluding the officers.  The FBI soon responds, only to find one bank teller dead, another wounded, and the bank's security guard shot four times, yet still alive.

A man is found suffocated in his Pennsylvania home, his checkbook, credit cards and vehicle appear to have been stolen.  Fingerprints from the victim identify a recent escapee from a minimum-security prison, as well as his girlfriend.  Investigators flag the dead man's credit cards, and are alerted when one is used in North Dakota.  The FBI is called in and joins another task force already assembled because of a suspected kidnapping.

In Wisconsin, a varsity athlete is blindfolded, gagged, and shoved into a van by four gunmen.  The kidnappers contact the victim's family and demand $30,000, but offer no instructions on how to transfer the money.  The victim's family contacts the police.  The boy's captors tell his family they have shot him, and will kill him if they do not receive their money.  At an agreed upon drop site, FBI agents approach the captor's vehicle, only to watch them flee and quickly be followed by authorities.

In 1991, the Safe Streets Task Force, a joint FBI / Washington D.C. Metropolitan Police Department organization, begins conducting an investigation into the violent activities of a local gang called the K Street Crew.  Gang members are suspected of involvement in several area homicides.  The FBI approaches several witnesses, hoping to convince them to testify against the gang members.  Seven potential witnesses are murdered during the course of the investigation.

In June of 2000, two gunmen rob a Seattle, WA bank, and flee on foot as officers chase them.  One of the gunmen is killed in a firefight with police, the other escapes after assaulting a family and using their home to hide.  The family helps FBI agents identify the man, who is suspected of several other robberies.  Seattle SWAT teams, working with the FBI, search the home of the assailant's mother, and find ammunition matching that used at the bank robbery.

A California bank manager panics and calls in the FBI after the door to his vault refuses to open.  Upon inspection, the vault has been blasted into from the ceiling, and over $2 million in valuables is gone.  When agents find no clues as to the robbers or their whereabouts in California, they send details of the crime to other FBI field offices.  It is not long before agents in Ohio are investigating a bank vault robbery that is strikingly similar to the California heist.

What followed was the bloodiest firefight in FBI history.

By December 1985, John Gotti had assumed his place as the new Don of the Gambino crime family in New York with the assassination of his boss, Paul Castellano. But he was also the ongoing obsession of Bruce Mouw, leader of an elite crew of FBI agents formed to bring down the Gambino family.  With the help and genius of his Special Projects Squad, bugs were planted in Gotti's most private meeting places.

In 1984, south Miami became the home for a sadistic serial killer.  Posing as a fashion photographer, Christopher Wilder lured young women from shopping malls with promises of fame and fortune.  Most ended up dead.  As the FBI closed in around him, Wilder took off on a cross-country murderous rampage.  The FBI added Wilder to their Most Wanted Fugitives program.  The chase was on, and Wilder ultimately lost.

Phone records showed a flood of calls to Black from his business rival just before the disappearance.

Agnes has an eventful time in Greece as Ali reveals the truth about himself to her. Later, she unexpectedly finds Valerie. Meanwhile, Iris decides to start anew, away from Ali.
An unexpected event cuts short Anton and Andeng's growing closeness.
After the distrastrous event, Andeng transfers to another project.

Hector tries to keep himself out of trouble by attempting to silence his henchman for good. However, he ends up in a precarious situation when his plan backfires. Busy trying to avoid being incriminated in Hector's schemes, Daniela becomes negligent of her responsibilities.

Carlos' insistence to help Romina leads to a severe argument with his wife. Unfortunately for Daniela, her problems continue when her selfish management of Camila Sardines leaves disgruntled employees in its wake.

After finding out that Santi is missing, Amelia blames Tiago for placing their son in danger. Sick with worry over her child, she confronts Corazon about her son's whereabouts. Rhian, Marcial, and Franco, on the other hand, decide to take Santi under their wing. Rhian then seizes the opportunity to persuade the child to turn his back on his father's syndicate. Tiago, meanwhile, refuses to accept defeat and formulates another nasty plan to take back his son.

Cinco reveals her true colors after Corazon got kidnapped by Tiago's henchmen. Holding on to the last loyal member of Mejor Cinco, Tiago is confident that his devious plan will eventually fall into place. Jessie, meanwhile, confronts Amelia after learning about her mother's abduction. Back in the lair of Tiago's henchman, Corazon faces a dilemma as her abductor forces her to contact her fugitive daughter. Rhian musters the courage to rescue her mother from the hands of the enemy.
